- Build a complete, playable 2D pixel-art roguelike platformer for phones and tablets about animal travelers managing homesickness while exploring biomes and towns.

## Requirements
- Homesickness rises from revisiting areas and hardships, falls from visiting sights, and resets in each new town.
- Towns offer purchasable wandering equipment; animals have distinct advantages and disadvantages.
- Support mobile/tablet touch controls and 16-bit-era graphics; build without clarification.

## Decisions
- Implemented a self-contained HTML Canvas game with hand-drawn pixel-style graphics and no external assets.
- Added three selectable travelers (fox, bear, rabbit), four biomes/towns, sights, puddles/thorns, shop equipment, and a final ending.

- Created a playable game in `index.html` with keyboard and touch controls, home/lost/ending states, town shop, and equipment effects.
- Checked JavaScript syntax with `node --check`.
- Opened the game in Playwright and saved screenshots; visual review was performed for title, mobile, and world views.

- `index.html`: Complete game implementation.
- `screenshots/title.jpg`: Title screen capture.
- `screenshots/mobile.jpg`: Mobile viewport capture.
- `screenshots/world.jpg`: Gameplay capture.

- Transform the existing Canvas platformer into **Wanderlust**, a procedurally generated, climb-focused wandering adventure with responsive movement, richer pixel-art visuals, and a wanderlust HUD.

## Requirements
- Rename the game “Wanderlust” and evoke SNES-era pixel art.
- Improve movement and jumping; make climbing lead to scenic views.
- Views are goals, not collectibles; berries and rare flowers restore wanderlust.
- Track homesickness and wanderlust internally as percentages; display only wanderlust.
- Sights and small wonders increase wanderlust; hardships decrease it.
- Generate each run procedurally so runs differ.
- Preserve travelers, biomes/towns, shops, keyboard/touch controls, and the ending where feasible.

## Decisions
- Continue with the self-contained HTML Canvas game in `index.html`; no external assets.
- Use a per-run random seed and a generated ascending route with a summit vista.

- Removed the leftover `TOWN` sign with a script replacement.

2. Run the game in Chromium via `playwright-cli` and exercise title, movement/climbing, vista transition, wonders, towns, and touch controls.
3. Fix issues discovered and rerun syntax and browser checks.

- `index.html`: Entire game implementation.
